summary: Approved after independent adversarial review bound the strict checked-in 31-row required-check subdocument to the exact ordered producer inventory and projected bindings, pinned the historic producer identities and optional Base-controlled identity, rejected malformed input and coordinated data drift all-or-zero, and preserved context 32 as inactive.

findings.summary: Coordinated 31-to-31 producer, ruleset, and workflow substitution passed equality until the final policy pinned the canonical historic 31-producer identity digest.

Deeply nested JSON could escape the fail-closed loader contract through RecursionError until both inventory and ruleset boundaries caught it and portable regression tests pinned empty evidence plus problems.

limitations: Candidate-owned validation can change the validator, identity digest, and tests together; candidate-independent enforcement requires a trusted old-base or base-controlled workflow.
Pinned producer identities do not attest workflow command semantics; unchanged identifiers can conceal a semantic no-op.
This slice does not prove the live ruleset, active workflow state, GitHub Actions App identity, admin no-bypass readback, or authenticated transport.
It validates the required-status-check subdocument rather than the complete outer ruleset, does not make all cross-file reads one immutable Git-object transaction, and does not authorize context 32.
